Jonathan Goforth
JON-uh-thun GOH-forth
proper noun
Jonathan from the Hebrew Yōnātān, “the LORD has given”; Goforth an English surname providentially suited to a man whose life answered the command “Go ye” into all the world.

📖 Biblical Definition

Jonathan Goforth (1859–1936) was a Canadian Presbyterian missionary to China and a leading instrument of revival in the northern provinces and in Manchuria. Born on an Ontario farm and converted as a young man, he was set ablaze for missions and went out with his wife Rosalind under the Canadian Presbyterian church, settling in Honan, a province others had judged too dangerous to enter. He gave himself to direct evangelism, opening his home and preaching tirelessly, and in the Boxer uprising of 1900 he and his family barely escaped with their lives, wounded and pursued, yet returned to the field as soon as the way was open. From 1908 onward the Lord poured out a remarkable awakening through his preaching of repentance and the cross, marked by deep conviction of sin, open confession, and restitution, after the pattern of true revival rather than worked-up emotion. Goforth held firmly to the inspiration of Scripture and the necessity of the new birth, and he attributed every awakening not to method but to the sovereign work of the Holy Ghost in answer to prayer. Late in life he labored on though blind, dictating and preaching to the last. He stands as a faithful son of the Great Commission, a man who took God at His word and saw multitudes turned from idols to the living God.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A Canadian Presbyterian missionary to China and Manchuria, used of God in widespread revival marked by conviction of sin.

expand to see more

JONATHAN GOFORTH, a Canadian Presbyterian missionary to China (1859–1936), pioneer of the work in Honan province.

He and his wife Rosalind barely escaped death in the Boxer uprising of 1900, yet returned to the field.

From 1908 he was used in a great awakening in China and Manchuria marked by conviction and confession of sin.

He ascribed every revival not to method but to the sovereign work of the Holy Spirit in answer to prayer.

He preached on though blind in his final years, faithful to the end (2Ti 4:7).

📖 Key Scripture

Zec 4:6 — "Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of the LORD unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts."

Act 3:19 — "Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord;"

2Ti 4:7 — "I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:"

Psa 85:6 — "Wilt thou not revive us again: that thy people may rejoice in thee?"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Goforth’s God-sent revivals are blurred by modern revivalism, which counterfeits the Spirit’s work with method, manipulation, and worked-up feeling.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The chief danger to Goforth’s legacy is not anti-missions ideology but a churchly counterfeit: the modern practice of manufacturing “revival” by emotional technique, crowd dynamics, and the planned altar call. Goforth would own none of it. He insisted that the awakenings he witnessed were not produced by his preaching but were the sovereign descent of the Holy Ghost upon prayer, attended by deep conviction of sin, honest confession, and costly restitution — fruits no method can manufacture (Zec 4:6). To trade his Spirit-wrought awakening for the salesman’s revivalism is to lose the very thing he stood for.

The lesson to recover is that true revival is the work of God, not the achievement of men, and that it comes by way of repentance and the preaching of the cross. Goforth’s ministry rebukes both the cessation of expectant prayer and the presumption of engineered excitement. He labored in season and out, took God at His word, and waited upon the Spirit; and when the times of refreshing came, he gave God all the glory. The church does well to seek that same outpouring on its knees rather than to imitate its outward effects by craft.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

His given name means “the LORD has given,” and his surname spelled out the command he obeyed: go forth.

expand to see more

Jonathan — Hebrew Yōnātān, “the LORD has given,” or “gift of the LORD.”

Goforth — an English surname that providentially echoed “Go ye therefore” (Mat 28:19).

The watchword of his life was the simple verb to go, in answer to the Lord’s command.

“Revival” comes of the Latin revivere, to live again, the very plea of Psalm eighty-five.

“Honan” named the inland province others shunned, where he planted the gospel.

Usage

"Jonathan Goforth pressed into Honan when other missionaries judged the province too perilous to enter."

"When revival came, Jonathan Goforth gave the glory to the Spirit and never to his own preaching."

"Blind in his last years, Jonathan Goforth still preached Christ wherever he was led."
